claim: The route criterion. Let K = {r, o, c} be a crossing knot at a gluing line L, with near points r, o leaving the set T of L's patterns and the far point c excluding the set E. (1) The route lemma (proved): K is generated from one-sided knots when it has a route. Either one point of L separates T from what the far point allows, or, for some ordered pair (y, y') of L's points and values (b, b') with T fixing y = b and E containing every pattern with (y, y') = (b, b'), one of two things holds. (i) r is tied to y and T also fixes y' = b' (eliminate y' from {r, o, y'} and {y, y', c}). (ii) r is tied to neither and {r, y, y'} excludes (r's value, b, not b'); eliminate y' from {r, y, y'} and {y, y', c}, then y. Degenerate ties put K in the base. (2) The converse (computation). The Fano plane was attached at a point of five grown plane pieces (10 to 14 points), with every removal inside the handle, every six-pattern plane gluing line and four far sides. The new crossing knots, exact up to three points, are exactly the three-point candidates with a handle point and no route: 1,500 knots in 182 creating cases, against 59,984 routed candidate instances, none new. (3) Creation is a function of (removal, far side, the plane piece's transfer between the handle's ports and L): 840 classes, none mixed.
